title: World of Warcraft Forever duyuruldu: Çıkış tarihi ve tüm detaylar
summary: Blizzard Entertainment, oyunu orijinal döneminde sabit tutan ve yeni içerikler sunan World of Warcraft Forever projesini BlizzCon 2026'da duyurdu.
body:
Blizzard Entertainment, BlizzCon 2026 etkinliğinde serinin merakla beklenen yeni sürümü **World of Warcraft Forever** duyurusunu gerçekleştirdi. Oyunculara yıllardır talep ettikleri "Classic Plus" deneyimini sunmayı hedefleyen yapım, şu anda beta aşamasında bulunuyor. Oyun, 4 Kasım tarihinde Windows PC ve Mac platformları için çıkış yapacak.

## World of Warcraft Forever neler sunuyor?
World of Warcraft Forever, oyunu The Burning Crusade öncesindeki dönemde tutarak herhangi bir genişleme paketinin ana yapıyı bozmasına izin vermiyor. Azami seviye sınırının 60'ta sabit kaldığı bu zaman kapsülünde, 2004 döneminin ruhunu korumak ana hedef olarak belirlendi. Blizzard'ın Polygon'a aktardığı detaylara göre oyunda sunulacak yenilikler şunlar:

* 1.000 adet yeni görev
* Yeni bölgeler ve zindanlar
* Yeni oynanabilir bir ırk
* Yaşam kalitesi geliştirmeleri

## Zamansız bir dünyada yavaş ilerleme
Polygon'a konuşan baş oyun tasarımcısı Tim Jones, ekibin odak noktasının son seviyeye aceleyle ulaşmak olmadığını, asıl amacın oyuncuların kendi hızlarında maceraya atılması olduğunu belirtti. Seviye atlama sürecini ve hikâye yolculuğunu merkeze aldıklarını aktaran Jones, eklenen her yeni içeriğin 2004 yılındaki orijinal tasarımlarla uyumlu hissettirmesi için çalışıldığını ifade etti.

**Neden önemli?** Yıllardır "Classic Plus" konseptini bekleyen Warcraft topluluğuna hitap eden bu adım, yoğun günlük temposu olan eski oyunculara acele etmeden oynayabilecekleri kalıcı bir dünya sunmayı amaçlıyor.

source_texts.title: World of Warcraft Forever's Plan to Bring 'Classic Plus' to New and Old Players
source_texts.summary: Blizzard reveals how World of Warcraft Forever will cater to 'Classic Plus' fans and newcomers who are jumping in 22 years later.
source_texts.text:
At BlizzCon 2026, Blizzard Entertainment revealed one of its most highly anticipated projects, World of Warcraft Forever. The third major iteration of Blizzard's landmark MMO will give Warcraft fans the "Classic Plus" version of WoW they've been pestering the developer about for years, even in the wake of 2019's World of Warcraft Classic.
World of Warcraft Forever is WoW in a time bubble, without the creep of major expansions and changes that have altered the beloved MMO over the past two decades. Forever will have new content — zones, quests, dungeons, and a new playable race — plus quality-of-life improvements that make the game distinct from the original World of Warcraft. But the developers behind the latest version of Blizzard's MMO are thinking very strategically about how to preserve what was great about WoW in its earliest years. They want to keep players curious, surprise them, and let them play World of Warcraft at their own (leisurely) pace.
At BlizzCon, Polygon spoke with Tim Jones, lead game designer, and Nora Valletta, lead software engineer, about how World of Warcraft Forever came to be, what the dev team's ambitions are for the throwback MMO, and how friendly the legendary game will be for newcomers. Read our full discussion below.
World of Warcraft Forever is currently beta testing and launches on Nov. 4 on Mac and Windows PC.
Polygon: You announced 1,000 new quests. With the design changes that have happened over the past 20 years in World of Warcraft, how is quest and dungeon design being approached in World of Warcraft Forever? Are people getting into the 2004-2006 headspace? What’s the approach?
Tim Jones: I think we have gone to great lengths to analyze what makes the era and Vanilla world special — the simplicity of objectives, of creature design. In that analysis, I think we have developed a set of core principles that apply to our game, the pacing of combat, and the complexity of quest design. In creating any quests, we look at Wetlands, for example, and we see a portion of the world that we say, "Hey, maybe there's a new objective that could exist in that location of the world and we want to create objectives there."
We want to make sure that whatever content we add feels like it could have always existed in 2004. We like to use the term “found photographs.” Ideally, if a 2004 player time traveled to now and was playing through the zone, it would feel like the objectives are simple and the creatures are the appropriate difficulty for the zone. We're not trying to complicate things unnecessarily but really stay true to that original vision of Vanilla WoW when we make these choices.
People who might've played in their teens, early 20s may not be able to sit and play WoW for four hours these days. Is that a consideration as well, in how you're approaching forever?
Jones: People have to adjust their mind space for the Vanilla game. I think if people can be satisfied with logging into their character, opening their quest log, and say, "Hey, I have 30 minutes, I have an hour, I have an hour and a half to play, I can get a couple quests done or I can go to the auction house and buy some materials and level up my professions a bit."
There's so many ways to have incremental progression on your character that's meaningful. The leveling experience and the leveling journey, it's long for a reason. We want players to have the ability to take it slow, not feel rushed. Our level cap is 60, and it's going to stay at 60. Some people want to rush to the end game because they're really excited about jumping into the raids, but that's really not what WoW Forever is about.
The leveling journey is so important. It's one of our core pillars: “journey before destination.” That's what makes the hardcore game set so beautiful is that it forces people to make that conscious decision to play the game in the moment. That's what we really hope that draws new players into the game is feeling like they can get a quarter of a level and level up some professions, progress through Elwynn Forest and get ready to move on to Westfall and for that to feel satisfying — for them not to feel rushed because there is no rush. We are in this for the long haul. We want to continue making content across all levels for the long haul.
Nora Valletta: I actually fit that demographic you described. I also don't have four hours every evening to necessarily sit down and play. And one of the things I do, at least in versions of [World of Warcraft] Classic where you have that slower gameplay loop, is I'll log in, maybe check my auctions, maybe farm some herbs. Sometimes just simply logging in and deciding you're going to do that one quest. There was a time I was like, "I'll just do this. I'll finish this one quest in the Wetlands." As I was leaving town, I saw someone trying to gank somebody else — I was on a PvP server — and I was like, "Well, I was gonna do that quest.” It just became like a 20-minute PVP session for me. And then I logged off there. And that's fun.
Jones: And you're not going to be “behind” for engaging in those things. If it takes you a hundred days to get to level 60, that's totally fine. There's meaningful progression through our legacy system that people can jump into and roll alts if that's their thing. You can grind a reputation.
I'm a dad. I have a seven-year-old and a five-year-old daughter. And when we're play testing in our internal alpha, I put the family to bed and then I can game for a couple hours. I can't necessarily play in a competitive raiding guild like my younger self might have wanted to, but it’s still fun. It was fun questing in the world, grouping up occasionally.
I’m curious about the lore considerations of expanding this era. Is there anything you're intentionally staying away from? This is its own contained space, right?
Jones: Yeah. We're in a time bubble. Timeline-wise, we exist in a space between Warcraft 3 and The Burning Crusade. The Molten Core hasn't released yet. We're perpetually living in the year or so that was the original Vanilla game. So there are things that are true: Arthas is still alive. Illidan is still alive.
When we're thinking about lore considerations, there are a couple different categories of content. There is the expected content that we can explore. There are places in the world that everyone knows exists, like Mount Hyjal. People know it's there, so it's not necessarily a surprise; people expect it. But it's exciting and new. No one's ever been to that part of the world during this period of time. So there's something exciting about that. Or it's even new, but feels like it could have been there the entire time.
Valletta: The Riverglades is a really good example of that.
Jones: Yeah. The lore that we're using for the Riverglades, we go back to the stories of Warcraft and Warcraft 2 like the sacking of Stormwind. We take elements of campaign missions from those old games — When the orcs were retreating and the humans were ch
